name: Electrification
description: At first, there was a legend related to the name of the problem, but now it's just a formal statement. You are given $$$n$$$ points $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ on the $$$OX$$$ axis. Now you are asked to find such an integer point $$$x$$$ on $$$OX$$$ axis that $$$f_k(x)$$$ is minimal possible. The function $$$f_k(x)$$$ can be described in the following way: form a list of distances $$$d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n$$$ where $$$d_i = |a_i - x|$$$ (distance between $$$a_i$$$ and $$$x$$$); sort list $$$d$$$ in non-descending order; take $$$d_{k + 1}$$$ as a result. If there are multiple optimal answers you can print any of them.
input_specification: The first line contains single integer $$$T$$$ ($$$ 1 \le T \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — number of queries. Next $$$2 \cdot T$$$ lines contain descriptions of queries. All queries are independent. The first line of each query contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$0 \le k \lt n$$$) — the number of points and constant $$$k$$$. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_1 \lt a_2 \lt \dots \lt a_n \le 10^9$$$) — points in ascending order. It's guaranteed that $$$\sum{n}$$$ doesn't exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: Print $$$T$$$ integers — corresponding points $$$x$$$ which have minimal possible value of $$$f_k(x)$$$. If there are multiple answers you can print any of them.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1175C — Electrification [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
